title: Loop Snapshot
statement: Implement `solve(n)`. Return a list of `n` integers `0, 1, ..., n-1`. This is the result of calling `n` functions created in a loop, each of which captured its own index. The bug to avoid is every function returning `n` or `n-1`. `n` may be 0.
hints: Build the functions with a default argument, `lambda i=i: i`, or append i into a new cell each iteration.
The results are 0 through n-1, not the final loop variable.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A lambda that reads the loop variable looks up that variable when it is called, which is after the loop has finished.

editorial: A lambda that reads the loop variable looks up that variable when it is called, which is after the loop has finished. Binding the current integer as a default argument, or storing it in a new list cell, snapshots the value from that iteration. Calling the functions then yields 0 through n-1.
